title: How to Build an E-Commerce App with AI (No Shopify Required)
summary: Build a custom e-commerce app — product catalog, cart, Stripe checkout, user accounts, order management — without a developer or a Shopify subscription.
body_markdown:
## The Database Schema (Auto-Provisioned)


Blink provisions the database automatically when you describe your app. For a standard e-commerce app, that means six tables working together:


E-commerce database schema provisioned automatically by Blink — products, orders, payments, and user accounts


Blink


Table Key columns


` users` id, email, password_hash, role, created_at


` products` id, name, description, price, images, category, stock


` variants` id, product_id, size, color, price_modifier, stock


` cart_items` id, user_id, product_id, variant_id, quantity


` orders` id, user_id, total, status, stripe_payment_id, created_at


` payments` id, order_id, stripe_intent_id, amount, status


None of these require you to open a database console, write SQL, or configure a connection string. Blink creates them from your description and keeps the schema in sync as you iterate.


You own the data. The database lives in your Blink project. Export it any time.


## Adding Stripe Payments


Stripe is the payment standard for custom e-commerce. The integration with Blink is straightforward:


1. Create a Stripe account at stripe.com (free to create, no monthly fee)
2. Get your live publishable and secret keys from the Stripe dashboard, then paste them into Blink when it asks — only live keys are accepted, not test ones
3. Blink saves your keys as project secrets and can register the necessary webhooks for you


Blink handles the payment intent creation, the checkout UI, and the webhook to confirm successful payments. You keep 100% of the Stripe processing fee transparency — no additional platform cut on top.


Compare that to Shopify: on the Basic plan, Shopify takes 2% of every transaction if you use a non-Shopify payment processor, on top of Stripe's own fees. On a store doing $50,000/month in sales, that's $1,000/month extra — more than the Shopify plan itself.


## Custom E-Commerce vs Shopify: When Each Makes Sense


This is not a verdict — it's a framework. Both approaches are genuinely good for different situations.


Custom e-commerce built with Blink vs Shopify: no transaction fees, no monthly platform cost, full ownership


Blink


**Shopify is the right call when:**


- You need a large app ecosystem (1,000+ Shopify-specific apps)
- You have complex fulfillment with 3PL providers that have Shopify connectors
- You need a team-managed store where non-technical staff do daily product management
- You're running high-volume dropshipping (Shopify's supplier ecosystem is unmatched)


**Building custom with AI wins when:**


- Your store needs logic Shopify can't support without expensive custom development
- You want to avoid transaction fees (2.9% + $0.30 + 0–2% platform fee adds up fast)
- You're building a marketplace or multi-vendor platform (Shopify doesn't support this natively)
- You want to embed a store inside an existing app or membership site
- You need a combined product — for example, a subscription SaaS that also sells physical products


The honest summary: Shopify is excellent for large catalogs with complex fulfillment. Custom-built wins when you need specific logic, no transaction fees, or total ownership of the user experience.


For more on building marketplaces and subscription-based commerce, see our guides on[building a marketplace app](https://blink.new/blog/how-to-build-a-marketplace-app) and[building a subscription app with Stripe](https://blink.new/blog/how-to-build-subscription-app-stripe) .
